This is a wonderful too & very good app. Harvest is the best. The desktop tool is solidly built, feature packed, and has personality without being cutesy with fun quotes about time built into the interface. 

The reporting is amazing and so easy to use. Project setup allows for a huge variety of customizations and option settings. The app works seamlessly with the online tool - so much so that I can start a timer for a call while I'm at my desk, get in my car and finish the call, then click the stop button whenever the call is over. Reporting functions are lacking in the app, but as I don't have to run reports on mobile, this isn't a big deal.

As a freelance consultant with multiple clients, and working Mom, I couldn't be nearly as professional or organized with out this tool. I've also used the tool in a team setting - where clear visibility into hours spent by person, task, and client are extremely helpful to staying within time limits and getting work done.

I can't tell you how the help desk support is, because I've never once had to call them. The tool works all the time and is simple to figure out.

HIGHLY recommend you check it out. It's definitely worth the small price tag for the functionality and performance.

reviews.text:
Harvest Time Tracker: A Handy Tool with Room for Voice Integration. I’ve been using Harvest Time Tracker for a while now, and overall, it’s a pretty solid tool for tracking work hours and managing projects. It’s super user-friendly, and I love how it helps me keep all my time organized, especially when juggling multiple projects.

One of the best features is how easy it is to track time with just a click. You can start and stop timers for different tasks or projects, making it simple to see where your time goes. There’s also a detailed reporting feature, so you can see exactly how much time you’ve spent on each project, which helps with billing clients or just understanding where your day went.

The integration options are also pretty cool. It syncs up nicely with other tools like Trello, Asana, and QuickBooks, which is super handy if you’re already using those for project management or accounting. This makes it easy to transfer data and keep everything in one place.

However, I think there’s room for improvement, especially with integrating voice assistants like Siri or Google. Imagine just saying, “Hey Siri, start tracking for the Creative Project 010” or “Hey Google, start time tracking for Web Design Project 0900.” That would save a ton of time and be a real game-changer, especially for those of us who are always on the go. It’d be even better if there were an Apple Watch app having that quick access on your wrist would make it super convenient when you’re in the middle of something and need to log your time without any hassle.

In summary, Harvest Time Tracker is a great tool for managing your time and projects efficiently. It’s easy to use, offers detailed reporting, and has some excellent integrations. But if they could add Siri or Google Assistant functionality and an Apple Watch feature, it would really take it to the next level. Highly recommend it for freelancers, agencies, or anyone who needs to keep their time organized!

Wish i had this 25 years ago. Legal billing is the bain of small and solo law firms.
I lost so much money even when i tried to keep track of time.
Could never find a program that was affordable and that would seamlessly track contingent hourly and flat fee work. Especially if that work was within the same project.

I am using Harvest now and frankly it is nearly seamless. I am picking up 20-40% more hours and the reports are clearly pointing out that some flat fee work is not carrying its load! Those fees will be adjusted upward in the new year and there will be a minor bump before that. Its also showing some contingent work is no longer covering the items being billed. So we will have to tighten case selection and demand expenses be prepaid. In the new fiscal year these cases will have to be taken as highbred fees a mix of hourly or flat fee tasks and contingent.

Finally Harvest has been enlightening in pointing out mission creep and keeping things on track. I now send weekly bills b/c they are so easy to assemble and email, eliminating a hated task for a secretary so she can focus on other tasks. The office no longer suffers serious “end of the month billing clog where little gets done outside of getting bukls out and collecting money.

From the client side, they love the detail and all but one like getting the bills more often. They are paying twice per month and by weekly billing it avoids “sticker shock” when a month goes by and the bill is high. They also like being able to track the projected hours.

By getting paid + 15 days rather than +30 or +60 we can see which clients are struggling earlier and either adjust the mission, change the billing or drop the client before we get “pot committed”. In all I LOVE THIS PROGRAM!!
